clue.text: Division of supermarket is into drink

indicators.note: into says the word is goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: A shopper muses that one supermarket section is given over entirely to alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division' suggests a company department, but it is a walkway between shelves; 'into' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Supermarket shelves are laid out in walkways, each one a section of the store.

clue.text: Modern day teacher's computer accessory

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era of dates
a don is a university teacher; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A present-day teacher owns some gadget for a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an extra device or program attached to a computer, an optional accessory.

clue.text: Improper accessory? Hold on, teachers work here

indicators.note: improper means not in the right form, so the letters are set out in another order

explanation.surface: Someone spots a dodgy accomplice and tells everyone to wait, then remarks on a staffroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Improper' rearranges the letters of the two fodder phrases together; the question mark disguises where the definition starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary school is the place of employment for teachers of pupils aged about 11 to 18.

clue.text: Bonnie Langford's style

indicators.note: the possessive says the name holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Praise for the flair of Bonnie Langford, the British actress and dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive does the work of a hidden-word signal: the name 'has' the answer inside it, at bonniE LANgford.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash or flair, a stylish confidence in how something is done.

clue.text: Puzzling clue for 3 riders found here

indicators.note: puzzling clue for says the answer itself, read as an instruction, would clue the answer to 3 down

parts.note: 3 refers to the answer to 3 down, ELAN

explanation.surface: A self-referential puzzle about where cyclists ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, CYCLE LANE moves letters round from one end to the other: LANE becomes ELAN, the answer to 3 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle lane is a strip of road reserved for bicycles, so that is where riders are.

clue.text: Band search round

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A musical group goes looking for another round of drinks or gigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small group of musicians, especially in jazz.

clue.text: Sing with old partner on the radio, wearing these?

indicators.note: something on the radio is heard, not seen, so the clue words are judged by their sound

parts.note: to croon is to sing softly, and an ex is an old partner, so together CROON EX

explanation.surface: Someone duets with a former spouse on air and wonders about the outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: CROON EX said quickly sounds like CREW NECKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Crew necks are jumpers with a round close-fitting collar, so the singers might be dressed in them.

clue.text: Liberal politician avoiding hail and whirlwind

indicators.note: avoiding means the greeting is kept out of the politician's name

parts.note: Ed Davey is leader of the UK Liberal Democrats
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

explanation.surface: A Lib Dem leader dodges a storm of hail and wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes AVE from ED DAVEY.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling current of air or water, a small whirlwind.

clue.text: Broadcast cunning horror film with Queen and Prince of Wales, say

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
craft means guile or cunning
Carrie is the 1976 horror film from Stephen King's novel
R, for regina, is Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A TV channel airs a crafty horror film featuring royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince of Wales' looks royal, as do Queen and Prince; it is HMS Prince of Wales, a Royal Navy ship.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Prince of Wales is a Royal Navy vessel with a flight deck, an example of this kind of warship.

clue.text: Shocking treatment following heartless email, just lost millions of voters

indicators.note: following says the treatment comes after the email's ends
heartless means the middle of the word email is dropped, leaving its ends

parts.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock

indicators.note: lost says the abbreviation for millions drops out of the word

parts.note: just in the sense of fair and right is moral
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: After an empty email campaign, a politician has shockingly lost millions of voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves EL from email; 'lost' takes M out of MORAL to leave ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral is the adjective for anything relating to an electorate and elections.

clue.text: Transfer a stolen design for spout

indicators.note: stolen means the letter a is taken away from the word

parts.note: a decal is a transfer, a design moved onto a surface
aim, as in purpose or intention, is a design

explanation.surface: Instructions to move a pirated design to a teapot's pouring part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stolen' takes the A out of DECAL to give DECL.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout is to speak at length in a pompous or rhetorical way, as one does when declaiming.

clue.text: English tend to provide for universal support

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in place of another, here the universal letter

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
U is the film classification for universal
to do is to provide, as in a cafe that does lunches

explanation.surface: The English are inclined to look after everyone with help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts DO in place of U in NURSE, giving NDORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to give public backing or approval, a synonym of supporting.

clue.text: Watershed moment?

parts.note: a turning point, but read literally the UK television watershed, after which adult content may be shown

explanation.surface: A pivotal turning point.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK the 'watershed' is 9pm, after which programmes unsuitable for children may be broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The hour of the British TV watershed is this time in the evening, so it is the moment itself.

clue.text: Trustworthy channel

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means reliable or dependable
a strait, a narrow channel of sea

explanation.surface: A TV station people can rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound advice is reliable; a sound is also a sea passage such as Plymouth Sound.

clue.text: Worry frequently with French and …

parts.note: et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: An unfinished sentence about often being anxious with the French, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues into 16 across: 'French and Saunders' is the British comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious and agitated, the same as worrying.

clue.text: Attempt to change eel's gender

indicators.note: changing the gender means the male letter is swapped for the female one

parts.note: a moray is a kind of eel

explanation.surface: An odd proposal to alter the sex of a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' with 'gender' swaps M (male) for F (female) in MORAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a sudden attempt or venture into some new activity.

clue.text: Deduce where American goes to generate terror

parts.note: where the American letter goes is in, giving IN

indicators.note: goes means the American letter leaves the word for terror

parts.note: fear is terror

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where an American would go to cause fear.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue really says A goes in FER to make FEAR; read the other way, FEAR without A is FER, and 'where' it goes is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning, which is what deducing is.

clue.text: … Saunders essentially going on second after support is rejected — it's famously hard

indicators.note: after says what follows comes behind the reversed support
going on says the middle letters are added onto the end
rejected means sent back, so the word for support is turned round

parts.note: aid means support or help
mo is a short moment, a second

indicators.note: essentially means at its heart, so the central letters of the name are used

explanation.surface: Continuing 13: Jennifer Saunders, of French and Saunders, carries on in a moment, tough as nails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rejected' turns AID into DIA; 'essentially' takes ND, the centre of SAUNDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamond is the hardest natural substance, the standard example of hardness.

clue.text: You can pack it with cooked bagel dough on top

indicators.note: on top in a down answer means the dough comes first

parts.note: duff is a stiff flour pudding made from dough, as in plum duff

indicators.note: cooked suggests something altered or fiddled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A bag you can fill with baked bagels topped with dough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges BAGEL to give ELBAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffel bag is a cylindrical holdall that travellers fill with belongings.

clue.text: Submission of study describing free movement about Europe

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the room surrounds the mixed letters

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

indicators.note: movement means the letters of free are moved about

parts.note: C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A dissertation on freedom of movement across the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' rearranges FREE as FERE; 'describing' wraps DEN round it after its first two letters, then 'about' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: Deference is respectful yielding to another's wishes, a form of submission.

clue.text: One's usually needled to learn Jennifer's missing first half

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: missing first half says the opening half of the name is dropped

parts.note: the name Jennifer is used as written; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone usually needles Jennifer to find out what she's lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing first half' keeps only the back half of JENNIFER, IFER.
explanation.definitionFit: Conifers are trees bearing needles instead of broad leaves, so they are needled.

clue.text: Ultimately we cull musk deer

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letters of the next three words are used

explanation.surface: A grim conclusion that we must kill a musk deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The elk is a large species of deer, a moose in North America.

clue.text: Wasp, perhaps, to hover next to drink

indicators.note: next to says the drink sits right after the hovering word

parts.note: to fly is to hover in the air
a half is half a pint of beer

explanation.surface: A wasp hovers near a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Wasp is a player for Wasps, an English rugby union club; the fly-half is a rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: A player for the Wasps rugby club could play in the number ten position, an example by club.

clue.text: Discontented servant not opening drawer to get plate with design

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of contents, so only the outside letters of servant stay
not opening means the first letter is left off

parts.note: a pencil is a drawer, something that draws

explanation.surface: An unhappy servant fails to open a drawer to get a decorated plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' is a chest's sliding box in the surface but someone or something that draws in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out sheet through which a design is painted or inked.

clue.text: Regularly visit hectic hotel to eat out

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word hectic

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pay frequent visits to a busy hotel to dine out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eat out' reads as dining at a restaurant, but it means corrode, as acid does.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to corrode a surface with acid, eating away the metal.

clue.text: Small farm regularly pursuing credit

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the word for regularly comes after

parts.note: oft is an old word for often, regularly

explanation.surface: A smallholding regularly chased for money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Simulated attack's outside, on board Iron Duke

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, so the iron's letters hold the pair

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: outside means the outer letters of attack, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A mock raid takes place aboard a ship named after the Iron Duke, Wellington.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'attack's' stands for 'is'. 'Iron Duke' looks like Wellington's nickname but splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Faked means feigned or counterfeited, as a simulated attack would be.

clue.text: Flag is recognised international symbol for starters

indicators.note: for starters means the opening letters of the following four words are taken

explanation.surface: A flag is a widely recognised international symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner; it is the plant also called a yellow flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a common name for the iris, especially the yellow wild species growing by water.

clue.text: Small farm's peaceful

parts.note: to till is to farm the land; the 's stands for 'is' as a link

explanation.surface: A smallholding is a tranquil place.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means calm and motionless, so quiet and peaceful.

clue.text: Worker gets fine for complaint

parts.note: a worker bee is the standard crossword worker
F is the abbreviation for fine, used on pencils

explanation.surface: An employee is fined and grumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is a grievance or grumble in informal usage.

clue.text: Retrospectively criticises game

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the word for criticises is read backwards

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does

explanation.surface: A reviewer pans a game looking back on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a children's card game where matching cards are called out.

clue.text: I disapprove of that list — revealing quality of some online searches

parts.note: boo is a cry of disapproval
to list is to lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A grumpy reaction to a list shows what kind of web search is being run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' reads as an itemised roll, but it is a ship's tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Boolean searches use AND, OR and NOT logic, a property of some search-engine queries.

clue.text: Expedition travelling west in khaki kit — no knapsacks

indicators.note: travelling west says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Explorers set off in khaki gear without rucksacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft had no hidden-word signal: 'in' supplies it. 'travelling west' reads IKITNOK right to left in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Kon-Tiki was Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 raft voyage across the Pacific, a famous expedition.

clue.text: Game with clubs over diamonds — profit not unknown — could spades help make your fortune here?

definitions.text: could spades help make your fortune here?

indicators.note: over says the game spreads across the letter for diamonds, holding it

parts.note: golf is the game played with clubs
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

indicators.note: not says the unknown letter is left out of the word

parts.note: yield is the profit or return on an investment
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A card game where clubs beat diamonds wonders whether spades will make you rich.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs, diamonds and spades all look like card suits; spades are digging tools in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldfield is a district where gold is mined, so digging with spades there might bring riches.

clue.text: Danger of a laundry detergent completely fading a little shirt

indicators.note: completely fading means vanishing entirely, so the letter is gone from the brand

parts.note: Persil is a well-known British washing powder brand

indicators.note: a little of the shirt means just its first letter

explanation.surface: A warning that a washing powder bleaches small shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Persil is a British laundry detergent brand. 'completely fading' removes S, the start of 'shirt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril means serious danger or risk.
